qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Tier-1 long-life permitted orebodies (Grasberg, Morenci), but pure price-taker in global commodity markets with 10-year median ROIC of 10.2% (< 12%).
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Proof of Moat & Pricing Power, REJECT). While FCX owns irreplaceable tier-1 natural resource assets including Grasberg and Morenci, it operates as a pure commodity price-taker on COMEX/LME spot pricing with zero independent pricing power. 10-year median ROIC is 10.2% (below the 12.0% hurdle), margins are highly cyclical, and earnings are exposed to capital-intensive smelter mandates and Indonesian resource nationalism.
qualitative.evidence: Freeport-McMoRan (FCX) is a leading global copper producer generating ~$25.5B–$25.9B in annual revenue (FY24–FY25), primarily from copper (~70–75%), gold (~15–20%), and molybdenum (~5%). Major assets include the Grasberg minerals district in Indonesia (PT-FI, 48.76% owned following forced 51% transfer to Indonesian state-owned MIND ID), Morenci and open pits across Arizona and New Mexico, and Cerro Verde (53.6%) in Peru. Despite owning world-class, geologically unique ore deposits, FCX has zero pricing power—realized prices are dictated entirely by COMEX and LME commodity spot markets. Multi-cycle capital efficiency fails the Munger quality hurdle: 10-year median GAAP ROIC is 10.2% (< 12.0%). Business economics are highly capital-intensive ($4.8B capex in 2024, $4.5B in 2025) and subject to heavy regulatory and resource-nationalism burdens, including billions invested in mandated domestic Indonesian smelting/refining facilities (Manyar smelter) and ongoing project debt. FCF generation fluctuates heavily with metal price cycles ($5.6B operating cash flow in 2025 vs $7.2B in 2024). Fails Munger compounder standards due to commodity price-taking and sub-hurdle cycle returns.
